# Commands

Every block on this page is what the command prints with `--help`, word for word (FlowCellar 0.1.0).
No command contacts the network and no command asks a question. Progress and notices go to standard
error, one line each; results go to standard output.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`scan`](#flowcellar-scan) | Build or update a library from one or more folders. |
| [`run`](#flowcellar-run) | One run folder: a bundle and one offline HTML report. |
| [`analysis`](#flowcellar-analysis) | One single-cell or spatial analysis folder: a bundle and one offline HTML report. |
| [`hub`](#flowcellar-hub) | Rebuild the static hub (hub/index.html) of a library. |
| [`serve`](#flowcellar-serve) | Show a library in the browser, served from this computer. |
| [`init`](#flowcellar-init) | Create an empty library and draft its flowcellar.toml. |
| [`discover`](#flowcellar-discover) | List the runs and files a scan would find; computes nothing. |
| [`ls`](#flowcellar-ls) | List the runs of a library. |
| [`show`](#flowcellar-show) | Inspect one run: verdict, checks, inputs or one section. |
| [`rm`](#flowcellar-rm) | Remove runs from a library (moved to its trash; the data folders are never touched). |
| [`recompute`](#flowcellar-recompute) | Judge runs again with the current limits; reads no input. |
| [`doctor`](#flowcellar-doctor) | Check the installation, a library and its roots. |
| [`validate`](#flowcellar-validate) | Check bundle files, or every bundle of a library. |
| [`schema`](#flowcellar-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of a bundle. |

## Global options

They go before the command name. `-L` is also accepted after it.

```text
Usage: flowcellar [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  FlowCellar: one QC library for all your Oxford Nanopore flow cells, wherever their runs are
  stored.

    flowcellar scan /place/one /place/two -L ~/flowcellar-library     build or update a library
    flowcellar serve ~/flowcellar-library --open                      look at it
    flowcellar run /path/to/run_folder -o qc/                         one run: a bundle and an offline report

  Nothing is copied from, moved in or written to the folders that are scanned.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR         The library folder (or the environment variable FLOWCELLAR_LIBRARY).
  --config FILE             A configuration file to use instead of the library's flowcellar.toml;
                            for 'run' without a library, the file whose limits judge the run.
  --jobs N                  Worker processes for reading large files; 0 chooses by itself.
                            [default: 0; x>=0]
  --threads N               Decompression threads for a BAM without an index.  [default: 4; x>=1]
  -v, --verbose             Say more (repeat for more).
  -q, --quiet               Warnings and errors only.
  --log-format [text|json]  Events on stderr as text lines or as JSON lines.  [default: text]
  --version                 Show the version and exit.
  -h, --help                Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  scan       Build or update a library from one or more folders.
  run        One run folder: a bundle and one offline HTML report.
  analysis   One single-cell or spatial analysis folder: a bundle and one offline HTML report.
  hub        Rebuild the static hub (hub/index.html) of a library.
  serve      Show a library in the browser, served from this computer.
  init       Create an empty library and draft its flowcellar.toml.
  discover   List the runs and files a scan would find; computes nothing.
  ls         List the runs of a library.
  show       Inspect one run: verdict, checks, inputs or one section.
  rm         Remove runs from a library (moved to its trash; the data folders are never touched).
  recompute  Judge runs again with the current limits; reads no input.
  doctor     Check the installation, a library and its roots.
  validate   Check bundle files, or every bundle of a library.
  schema     Print the JSON Schema of a bundle.
```

## flowcellar scan

```text
Usage: flowcellar scan [OPTIONS] [ROOTS]...

  Find the runs under ROOTS, add them to the library DIR and judge them. Creates the library when
  DIR does not exist and remembers the roots; without ROOTS the remembered ones are scanned again.

    flowcellar scan /data/minknow /data/projects -L ~/flowcellar-library     the first scan: creates the library
    flowcellar scan -L ~/flowcellar-library                                  later: looks for what is new
    flowcellar scan /another/folder -L ~/flowcellar-library                  adds a folder and scans all of them

  Nothing is copied from, moved in or written to ROOTS. Verdicts from the small files come first;
  the reads are counted afterwards, newest runs first, inside the time box, and a later scan goes on
  where this one stopped. Exit code 5: finished, but a root or a file was skipped.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR   The library folder. Required.
  --name TEXT         Name of the library, when this scan creates it.
  --tier [1|2|all]    1: run health only. 2: read data only. all: both, run health first.  [default:
                      all]
  --only ID           Only these run keys or flow cell ids (repeatable).
  --since DATE        Only runs started on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
  --time-box MIN      Stop starting new passes after this many minutes; 0 = no limit. [default: 240,
                      or [scan] time_box_minutes]  [x>=0]
  --read KIND         Of the read data, read only this kind of large file in this scan (repeatable):
                      bam, tables (annotated read tables) or analyses (the per-read tables of
                      single-cell and spatial analyses). [default: all three, in this order]
  --quick             Verdicts from the small files only: count no reads and read no read data in
                      this scan.
  --wait / --no-wait  Wait for another scan of this library to finish, or exit with code 5.
                      [default: wait when not on a terminal]
  --dry-run           Say what would be done and write nothing.
  --retry-failed      Try again the inputs whose last pass ended in an error.
  --force             Recompute even where nothing changed.
  --no-index          Do not rebuild the index.
  --no-hub            Do not rewrite the hub.
  -h, --help          Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar run

```text
Usage: flowcellar run [OPTIONS] RUN_DIR [TIER2_PATHS]...

  Read one MinKNOW run folder RUN_DIR (and read-data files under TIER2_PATHS), write
  <prefix>.fcb.json.gz and <prefix>.flowcellar.html into --outdir, and with -L add the run to a
  library.

Options:
  -o, --outdir DIRECTORY          Where the bundle and the report are written.
  --prefix TEXT                   File name prefix. [default: the run key]
  --input ROLE=PATH               A read-data file or folder with its role, for example
                                  dorado.bam=bam_pass/ (repeatable).
  --sample-sheet FILE             Basecaller sample sheet (barcode, alias).
  --quick                         Stop after the quick report: do not count the reads.
  --assay [gdna|amplicon|cdna_pcr|cdna_direct|direct_rna]
                                  State the assay instead of detecting it.
  --flow-cell-use N               Which loading of the flow cell this is (1 = first use, stated).
                                  [x>=1]
  --reused                        The flow cell was used before (the same as --flow-cell-use 2).
  --flow-cell-check-pores N       Pore count of MinKNOW's flow cell check before loading.  [x>=0]
  --baseline-group LABEL          Comparison group label for this run.
  --no-report                     Write the bundle only.
  --no-bundle                     Write the report only.
  --deterministic                 Pin times and leave timings out: identical inputs give identical
                                  bytes.
  --fail-on [warn|fail|incomplete]
                                  Exit with code 3 when the verdict is at or above this level.
  -L, --library DIR               The library folder.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar analysis

```text
Usage: flowcellar analysis [OPTIONS] ANALYSIS_DIR

  Read one analysis folder ANALYSIS_DIR: a Space Ranger outs/ folder (or the folder that holds it),
  or the output folder of wf-single-cell (or one sample folder inside it). Writes <id>.fcb.json.gz
  and <id>.flowcellar.html into --outdir, and with -L adds the analysis to a library.

    flowcellar analysis spaceranger/outs -o qc/
    flowcellar analysis wf-single-cell/ -o qc/ --run TST00001
    flowcellar analysis spaceranger/outs -L ~/flowcellar-library

  The analysis has a verdict of its own. It never changes the verdict of a flow cell run.

Options:
  -o, --outdir DIRECTORY   Where the bundle and the report are written.
  --prefix TEXT            File name prefix. [default: the analysis id]
  --run FLOWCELL[@RUNID8]  A flow cell run the reads came from, when the files do not say
                           (repeatable).
  --sibling DIR            The analysis of the same reads by the other pipeline (a Space Ranger
                           outs/ folder, or a wf-single-cell sample folder).
  --no-sibling             Do not read the analysis of the same reads by the other pipeline with it.
  --label TEXT             The name to show instead of the pipeline's sample id.
  --no-read-pass           Do not read the workflow's per-read table (minutes): read counts come
                           from its report.
  --map-um [64|32]         Bin size of a Visium HD map, in µm.  [default: 64]
  --no-tissue-image        Leave the grey tissue picture out of a Visium HD map.
  --no-report              Write the bundle only.
  --no-bundle              Write the report only.
  --fail-on [warn|fail]    Exit with code 3 when the verdict is at or above this level.
  -L, --library DIR        The library folder.
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar hub

```text
Usage: flowcellar hub [OPTIONS] LIBRARY

  Write LIBRARY/hub/index.html, the index and one data file per run. Scan does this by itself; this
  command only rebuilds the page.

Options:
  --no-sidecars  Write the page and the index only; runs then open under 'flowcellar serve' only.
  --reports      Also write one offline report per run into reports/ (not for analyses: 'flowcellar
                 analysis DIR -o OUT' writes theirs).
  --open         Open the hub in the default browser.
  -h, --help     Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar serve

```text
Usage: flowcellar serve [OPTIONS] LIBRARY

  Serve the hub of LIBRARY: the same files 'flowcellar hub' writes, read-only. Stops with Ctrl-C.

  Only this computer can reach it unless --allow-lan is given. There is no editing and no password.

Options:
  --host TEXT           Address to listen on. [default: 127.0.0.1, or [serve] host]
  --port INTEGER RANGE  [default: 8737, or [serve] port]  [1<=x<=65535]
  --allow-lan           Accept requests from other computers (needed with a --host other than
                        127.0.0.1).
  --open                Open the hub in the default browser.
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar init

```text
Usage: flowcellar init [OPTIONS] LIBRARY

  Optional: 'flowcellar scan' creates a library by itself. Use init to shape flowcellar.toml first.

  Writes LIBRARY/flowcellar.toml with every section and its default. With --from-scan the roots are
  filled in and the read-data file patterns that the folders suggest are added as comments to check.
  Then edit the file and run: flowcellar scan -L LIBRARY

Options:
  --from-scan ROOT  Walk this folder and propose roots and file patterns from what is there
                    (repeatable). Computes nothing.
  --name TEXT       Name of the library.
  -h, --help        Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar discover

```text
Usage: flowcellar discover [OPTIONS] [ROOTS]...

  Walk ROOTS (or the roots of the library given with -L) and print run folders, raw-only folders,
  look-alikes and read-data files. Nothing is read beyond identity evidence and nothing is written.

  With -L the library's flowcellar.toml gives the file patterns and the project rule of each root;
  ROOTS then limits the walk to those folders.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR          The library folder.
  --explain                  For every file: the run it would be attached to, by which evidence.
  --format [table|tsv|json]  How to print the result.  [default: table]
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar ls

```text
Usage: flowcellar ls [OPTIONS]

  One line per run, newest first: run key, start, verdict, the stored headline.

    flowcellar ls -L DIR --where 'status:warn,fail after:2026-03'
    flowcellar ls -L DIR --where 'project:alpha reads:>1M' --columns id,started,reads,gb,project --format tsv

Options:
  -L, --library DIR          The library folder. Required.
  --where EXPR               Filter in the hub's search grammar, for example 'status:warn
                             fc:TST00001'.
  --columns LIST             Comma-separated column ids of the index.
  --sort COLUMN              Column to sort by; a leading '-' reverses. [default: -started]
  --analyses                 List the single-cell and spatial analyses of the library instead of its
                             runs.
  --format [table|tsv|json]  How to print the result.  [default: table]
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar show

```text
Usage: flowcellar show [OPTIONS] RUN_ID

  RUN_ID is a run key, or a flow cell id when the library holds one run of it; or the id of an
  analysis (an_...), as "flowcellar ls --analyses" lists them.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR  The library folder. Required.
  --inputs           The input files with role, state and link.
  --status           Every check with its outcome and sentence.
  --section ID       The summary of one section, for example fc or len.
  --json             Print the composed bundle (or the chosen part) as JSON.
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar rm

```text
Usage: flowcellar rm [OPTIONS] RUN_IDS...

  Moves bundle, status, card, state, sidecar and report of each run to trash/ and writes a
  tombstone, so the next scan does not add it again. 'flowcellar run RUN_DIR -L DIR' adds a run back
  on purpose.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR  The library folder. Required.
  --purge            Delete instead of moving to trash/.
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar recompute

```text
Usage: flowcellar recompute [OPTIONS] [RUN_IDS]...

  Each run is judged against its history as of its own start; no bundle is rewritten.

  Use it after changing limits in flowcellar.toml. A run that was judged before older runs were
  added keeps its verdict unless --rebaseline is given.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR  The library folder. Required.
  --status-only      Rewrite status files and cards only (the one mode of this build).
  --rebaseline       Also take the history as the library holds it now.
  --all              Every run of the library.
  --where EXPR       Runs matching this search.
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar doctor

```text
Usage: flowcellar doctor [OPTIONS]

  Versions and optional packages; the built viewer and its hashes; for a library: marker, layout,
  lease, whether each root answers, file-system type, and the time of one directory listing per
  root.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR     The library folder.
  --format [text|json]  How to print the result.  [default: text]
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar validate

```text
Usage: flowcellar validate [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

  PATHS are bundle files (*.fcb.json.gz), reports are not read. A library folder (as a path, or with
  -L) checks all its bundles with their status files composed in. Exit code 7 when anything fails.

Options:
  -L, --library DIR     The library folder.
  --format [text|json]  How to print the result.  [default: text]
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.
```

## flowcellar schema

```text
Usage: flowcellar schema [OPTIONS]

  Prints the schema this FlowCellar writes (flowcellar.model.schema.schema_text).

Options:
  --schema-version X.Y.Z  A published schema version. [default: the current one]
  --list                  List the schema versions in this package.
  -h, --help              Show this message and exit.
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | unexpected internal error (`-v` prints the traceback) |
| 2 | usage error: an unknown option, a missing argument |
| 3 | the verdict is at or above the level given with `run --fail-on` |
| 4 | an input was not found, not readable or not recognised |
| 5 | finished, but a root, a run or a file was skipped or failed |
| 6 | library problem: not a library, a newer layout, not writable |
| 7 | validation failed |
| 8 | a resource limit was exceeded |
| 130 | interrupted; what was finished is kept |

## Searching: `ls --where`

`ls --where` uses the search of the hub's Runs table. Every term must match. A plain word matches any
text of a run (ids, names, kit, project, samples); `field:value` matches one column, with a comma for
"any of"; numbers take comparisons and units; a `-` in front excludes.

```text
status:warn,fail          runs with a warning or a failure
kit:SQK-PCB114-24         one kit
project:alpha             one project
yield:>50gb               more than 50 Gb estimated
after:2026-01-01          started on or after a date;  year:2026  last:90d
-status:pass              everything that did not pass
```

## Files a command writes

| File | Written by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>.fcb.json.gz` | `run` | the bundle of one run with its verdict: gzip-compressed JSON that follows the schema `flowcellar schema` prints |
| `<prefix>.flowcellar.html` | `run`, `hub --reports` | one self-contained page; opens from a file and makes no request |
| `<library>/hub/index.html` | `scan`, `hub` | the library's pages; `index.js` and `data/<run key>.js` beside it hold the data |
| everything else under `<library>/` | `scan`, `run -L`, `rm`, `recompute` | see [The library](library.md) |
